project.name: streaming-xp-app
project.description: An Angular 19 SSR app demonstrating streaming Gemini AI responses via the Google Gen AI SDK (@google/genai): an Express endpoint (GET /api/stream-response) pipes generateContentStream chunks to a browser component that renders them incrementally using Angular 19 resource() over a ReadableStream.

nodes.name: app.component.ts
nodes.summary: Root Angular component that fetches a streaming Gemini response from `/api/stream-response` and progressively renders the accumulated text using the Angular 19 `resource` API with an async ReadableStream iterator.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Angular 19 experimental `resource` API with a `stream` factory returning a signal, combined with a native `ReadableStream` async iterator — a pattern that replaces RxJS observables for streaming data binding.

nodes.name: AppComponent
nodes.summary: The application's root component; owns the streaming resource that incrementally accumulates decoded text chunks from the backend SSE/streaming endpoint into a signal-backed `characters` property.

nodes.name: main.server.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side bootstrap entry point that exports a default `bootstrap` function for Angular Universal SSR, wiring `AppComponent` with the server-specific application configuration.

nodes.name: main.ts
nodes.summary: Client-side bootstrap entry point that calls `bootstrapApplication` with `AppComponent` and the browser application configuration, initializing the Angular app in the browser.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Angular CLI-generated project overview for streaming-xp-app, covering development server setup, code scaffolding commands, build instructions, unit and e2e test execution, and links to Angular CLI documentation.

nodes.name: angular.json
nodes.summary: Angular workspace configuration for streaming-xp-app defining the SSR-enabled application build (with src/server.ts as the SSR entry), production and development build targets, bundle size budgets, and the dev server builder.
nodes.languageNotes: SSR is enabled via outputMode: server and an explicit ssr.entry pointing at src/server.ts. Schematics are configured to skip test generation (skipTests: true) for all Angular schematic types.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: NPM manifest declaring Angular 19, @google/genai SDK, Express, and @angular/ssr as runtime dependencies, with a serve:ssr:streaming-xp-app script to launch the built SSR server from dist/.

nodes.name: tsconfig.app.json
nodes.summary: Application-scoped TypeScript configuration extending the base tsconfig.json, explicitly listing src/main.ts, src/main.server.ts, and src/server.ts as compilation entry files for the Angular SSR build.
nodes.languageNotes: The files array explicitly enumerates the three entry points (browser bootstrap, server bootstrap, and Express SSR server) rather than relying on a glob include, which is the recommended Angular pattern.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Base TypeScript compiler configuration enabling strict mode, ES2022 target with bundler module resolution, experimental decorators, and Angular-specific strict compiler options including strictTemplates and strictInjectionParameters.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses moduleResolution: bundler (introduced in TypeScript 5.0) suited for Angular's esbuild-based build pipeline. Angular compiler options enable strict template checking and strict injection parameter validation.

nodes.name: app.config.server.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side Angular application configuration that merges the base client config with SSR providers (server rendering and server routing), exporting a unified config consumed by the SSR bootstrap.

nodes.name: app.config.ts
nodes.summary: Root Angular application configuration supplying core providers: HTTP client with fetch backend, zone-based change detection, router with client routes, and client hydration with event replay for SSR.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Angular 19 standalone providers API; provideClientHydration with withEventReplay enables SSR hydration.

nodes.name: app.routes.server.ts
nodes.summary: Defines server-side Angular SSR route configuration, setting all routes to Prerender render mode for static output generation.

nodes.name: app.routes.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the client-side Angular router routes array, currently empty as no additional routes are defined beyond the root.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Root HTML shell for the StreamingXpApp Angular application, containing the app-root bootstrapping element and base metadata.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Express server integrating Angular SSR with a Gemini streaming API endpoint; serves static assets, handles SSR rendering via AngularNodeAppEngine, and streams Gemini 2.0 Flash responses to the client over HTTP.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @google/genai generateContentStream with async iteration to stream chunks directly to the HTTP response without buffering.

nodes.name: styles.css
nodes.summary: Global CSS stylesheet for the Angular application, currently minimal (1 line).

nodes.name: GET /api/stream-response
nodes.summary: Express GET endpoint that streams a Gemini 2.0 Flash model response chunk-by-chunk to the HTTP client, using generateContentStream for real-time AI output delivery.

layers.name: Frontend UI
layers.description: The browser-rendered surface of the streaming demo: the root Angular component that opens a ReadableStream to the Gemini endpoint and progressively renders accumulated text chunks, together with the HTML shell and global stylesheet.

layers.name: Streaming Backend
layers.description: The Express SSR server and its Gemini streaming endpoint, which call @google/genai generateContentStream and pipe AI response chunks directly to the HTTP client while also serving static assets and delegating Angular SSR rendering.

layers.name: App Bootstrap & SSR Configuration
layers.description: Angular application wiring for both browser and server environments: client and server bootstrap entry points, provider configurations (HTTP, hydration, zone change detection), and client/server route definitions that control SSR prerendering behavior.

layers.name: Build & Project Configuration
layers.description: Root-level configuration files that govern the Angular workspace build, NPM dependencies, and TypeScript compilation — including SSR output mode settings, bundle budgets, and strict type-checking options.

layers.name: Documentation & Tooling
layers.description: Project documentation and analyzer tooling support files: the CLI-generated README covering setup and build commands, and the Understand-Anything ignore configuration scoping which files are included in codebase analysis.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md provides the project name, CLI version, and the commands needed to run and build the app. It establishes the development baseline: `ng serve` on port 4200 for local development and `ng build` for production output. Reading this first anchors every subsequent file in its operational context.

tour.title: Browser Bootstrap
tour.description: src/main.ts is the client-side entry point — it calls Angular's `bootstrapApplication` with `AppComponent` and the browser-specific provider config. This is the first file the browser executes, so understanding it reveals how the Angular runtime is initialized before any UI renders.
tour.languageLesson: Angular 19 uses standalone bootstrapping (`bootstrapApplication`) instead of NgModule-based `platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule()`. This means every provider is registered directly through the `ApplicationConfig` object rather than through a root module.

tour.title: HTML Shell & App Root
tour.description: src/index.html is the static HTML document the browser loads first, containing the `<app-root>` element that Angular replaces with the rendered component tree. It is the physical mounting point that connects the browser's DOM to the Angular bootstrap in main.ts.

tour.title: Application Providers & Routing
tour.description: app.config.ts wires the core Angular providers — HTTP client with fetch backend, zone-based change detection, client-side router, and SSR hydration with event replay. app.routes.ts holds the routes array (currently empty, meaning the root component handles everything). Together they define the runtime environment that `AppComponent` operates within.
tour.languageLesson: `provideClientHydration(withEventReplay())` is an Angular 19 SSR feature: after the server pre-renders HTML, the browser replays user interactions that occurred before hydration completed, avoiding lost clicks or keystrokes during the hand-off.

tour.title: Streaming UI Component
tour.description: app.component.ts is the core of the demo — it uses Angular 19's experimental `resource` API with a `stream` factory to open a `ReadableStream` to `/api/stream-response` and progressively accumulates decoded text chunks into a signal-backed `characters` property. Each chunk triggers reactive re-rendering as the AI response arrives token by token, with no RxJS required.
tour.languageLesson: The Angular `resource` API's `stream` option accepts a factory returning a `Signal<T>` updated incrementally. Combined with a `ReadableStream` async iterator, this replaces the classic `HttpClient` + RxJS `scan` pattern: the component reacts to each pushed chunk without subscribing to an observable.

tour.title: Express Server & Gemini Streaming Endpoint
tour.description: src/server.ts is the Express server that plays two roles simultaneously: it serves static build artifacts and delegates Angular SSR rendering via `AngularNodeAppEngine`, and it exposes `GET /api/stream-response` — the endpoint that calls `@google/genai`'s `generateContentStream` and pipes Gemini 2.0 Flash output chunk-by-chunk directly into the HTTP response. This is the backend half of the streaming path that `app.component.ts` reads from.
tour.languageLesson: `generateContentStream` returns an async iterable; iterating it with `for await...of` and writing each `chunk.text` to `res.write()` streams tokens to the browser without buffering the full response — keeping time-to-first-token low regardless of total response length.

tour.title: SSR Bootstrap & Server Configuration
tour.description: main.server.ts is the server-side counterpart to main.ts: it exports a `bootstrap` function consumed by Express's `AngularNodeAppEngine` to render the Angular component tree on the server before sending HTML to the client. app.config.server.ts merges the base client providers with SSR-specific ones (server rendering, server routing), and app.routes.server.ts sets all routes to Prerender mode — meaning pages are rendered at build time for fast initial delivery.

tour.title: Build & TypeScript Configuration
tour.description: angular.json is the Angular workspace configuration that declares the SSR build target, points `ssr.entry` at src/server.ts, sets bundle size budgets, and enables the esbuild-based builder. tsconfig.json and tsconfig.app.json set up strict TypeScript compilation with `bundler` module resolution and explicitly enumerate the three entry points (main.ts, main.server.ts, server.ts) so the compiler processes browser, SSR, and Express code in a single pass.
tour.languageLesson: `moduleResolution: bundler` (TypeScript 5.0+) tells the compiler to resolve modules the way esbuild does rather than following Node.js CJS rules. This is required for Angular 19's esbuild pipeline and allows importing `.js` extensions in source while still compiling `.ts` files.

tour.title: Dependencies & NPM Scripts
tour.description: package.json declares the key runtime dependencies that make this demo possible: Angular 19, `@google/genai` (the Gemini SDK), `express`, and `@angular/ssr`. The `serve:ssr:streaming-xp-app` script launches the compiled Express server from `dist/`, which is the production path that wires together every layer explored in this tour.
